prompt: What does this sign require you to do?
choices: Slow down and keep going if no other vehicles are coming
Stop completely, yield, then go when it is safe
Stop only if other vehicles are already in the intersection
Slow down and yield, but stop only if traffic is close
explanation: This sign always requires a complete stop, even when the road looks empty. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic and go only when it is safe. Slowing without stopping is a violation.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What must you do when you see this sign?
choices: Always come to a complete stop, even when no traffic or pedestrians are near
Keep your speed, because cross traffic and pedestrians must yield to you
Speed up so you can merge ahead of the approaching traffic
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others with the right-of-way go first
explanation: This downward-pointing triangle means yield: slow down, check for traffic and pedestrians, and stop if needed to let them go first. A full stop is required only when traffic or pedestrians make it necessary.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You reach this sign and no vehicles, bicyclists or pedestrians are coming. What should you do?
choices: Come to a full stop anyway, then proceed
Wait for another driver to wave you through
Proceed carefully without stopping
Stop and sound your horn before proceeding
explanation: Unlike a stop sign, a yield sign does not require a stop when the way is clear. You only need to stop when other road users with the right-of-way are close enough to be a hazard.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: This plaque is mounted below a yield sign at the entrance to a one-lane bridge. What does it tell you?
choices: Drivers coming toward you on the bridge must wait and yield to you
Let oncoming vehicles go first before you enter the bridge
Traffic on the bridge ahead moves in only one direction at a time
Yield only to vehicles that approach the bridge from your right side
explanation: The plaque means you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming (opposing) traffic, such as on a one-lane bridge or underpass. It does not make the road one-way.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: This plaque is mounted under a stop sign. What does it tell you?
choices: Traffic from every direction must stop at this intersection
Only traffic on the side road must stop; the main road does not
You may turn right without stopping if the way is clear
Cross traffic does not have to stop, so wait for a gap
explanation: The plaque means every approach to the intersection has a stop sign (an all-way stop). After stopping, the first vehicle to arrive goes first.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: At an intersection where every stop sign has this plaque, you and another car stop at the same moment. The other car is on your right. Who should go first?
choices: You, because you are on the left
Whichever car is larger
Whichever driver turns on a signal first
The car on your right
explanation: At an all-way stop, the first vehicle to stop goes first. If two vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign tell drivers?
choices: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles before stepping into this crosswalk
Drivers must stop at the line every time, even when no one is crossing
Yield to crossing pedestrians at the line, back from the crosswalk
Pedestrians may cross only in the direction the arrow is pointing
explanation: This sign marks the yield line set back from an unsignalized crosswalk. Yielding back at that line lets drivers in other lanes see the pedestrian, helping prevent a "multiple-threat" crash.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: This sign stands in the middle of the street at a crosswalk. What does it remind drivers to do?
choices: Stop every time, even when the crosswalk is empty
Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Watch for a school bus stop ahead
Keep to the left of the sign only
explanation: This in-street sign reminds drivers that the law requires them to yield to pedestrians within the crosswalk. It does not require a stop when the crosswalk is empty.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: A pedestrian is walking in the crosswalk where this in-street sign is placed. What must you do?
choices: Stop and let the pedestrian cross
Slow down and steer around the pedestrian
Sound your horn, then continue carefully
Stop only if a crossing guard is present
explanation: This sign version tells drivers that the law requires them to stop for pedestrians within the crosswalk. Driving around a pedestrian who is crossing is never safe.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: The recommended speed for a curve or hazard ahead is 50 mph
You must drive at exactly 50 mph whenever traffic allows it
The lowest speed allowed on this road is 50 mph
The maximum legal speed here in good conditions is 50 mph
explanation: A white rectangular speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. Yellow signs with speeds are advisory, and minimum speeds are shown separately.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (speed limit signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, TX p.34)

prompt: It is raining heavily and you pass this sign. Which statement is true?
choices: You may always drive 50 mph because it is the posted limit
The limit does not apply in bad weather
You may need to drive slower than 50 mph to be safe
You must drive at least 50 mph to keep up with traffic
explanation: Every state has a basic speed rule: you must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions. In rain, fog or heavy traffic, a safe speed may be well below the posted limit.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (speed limit signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, TX p.34)

prompt: This plaque is mounted below a speed limit sign. What does it mean?
choices: Trucks must go at least 40 mph
Trucks may not go faster than 40 mph
Trucks are banned for the next 40 miles
Cars must slow to 40 mph when passing trucks
explanation: This plaque sets a lower maximum speed that applies to trucks. Other vehicles follow the main speed limit sign above it.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (speed limit signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, TX p.34)

prompt: This plaque is mounted below a speed limit sign. What does it mean?
choices: The speed limit at night is 45 mph
Only trucks are limited to 45 mph
The minimum speed is 45 mph
45 mph is the recommended speed in fog
explanation: The white-on-black plaque gives a lower speed limit that applies at night, when visibility is reduced.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (speed limit signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, TX p.34)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: Cars may go up to 50 mph, but trucks are limited to 30 mph or less
The limit is 50 mph during the day and 30 mph at night
The speed limit drops from 50 mph to 30 mph just ahead
Normally, drive no faster than 50 mph and no slower than 30 mph
explanation: This sign shows both a maximum and a minimum speed. Driving far below the flow of traffic can be as dangerous as speeding, but you may go slower than the minimum when conditions make it unsafe.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (speed limit signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, TX p.34)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: You must turn right here
The road ahead turns sharply to the right
You may not turn right here
Right turns are allowed only on a green arrow
explanation: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is prohibited. Here, right turns are not allowed.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: You want to turn left at an intersection where this sign is posted. What should you do?
choices: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Do not turn left here; use another route
Turn left only when a green arrow is shown
Turn left only if no oncoming traffic is in sight
explanation: The red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow means left turns are not allowed at this location, whatever the signal shows. Continue on and use another route.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: Which movement is allowed at the intersection where this sign is posted?
choices: Going straight
Turning right only
Turning left after stopping
Making a U-turn
explanation: This sign prohibits all turns - left, right and U-turns - so you must continue straight through the intersection.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign prohibit?
choices: Turning left onto the cross street at this spot
Entering a one-way street from the wrong end
Backing up on the roadway
Turning around to go back the way you came
explanation: The slashed U-shaped arrow means U-turns are not allowed here. Left turns are still permitted unless another sign prohibits them.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What is prohibited where this sign is posted?
choices: U-turns only; left turns are allowed
Left turns only; U-turns are allowed
Left turns and U-turns
Right turns and U-turns
explanation: This sign combines the left-turn and U-turn symbols under one red slash, so neither movement is allowed.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: This is a one-way street, so you may only go straight ahead
You may not continue straight through the intersection
Do not pass the vehicle ahead of you
Left turns are not allowed, but right turns are
explanation: A red slash over a straight-ahead arrow means through movement is prohibited, so you must turn. Compare it with the "straight only" lane sign, which has no slash.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: This sign is posted over a lane at an intersection. What does it mean?
choices: Vehicles in this lane must go straight
Vehicles in this lane may go straight or turn
The street ahead is one-way
This lane ends after the intersection
explanation: A lane-use arrow with the word ONLY means the movement shown is the only one allowed from that lane - here, straight ahead.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: You want to go straight at the next intersection, and this sign is over the lane you are in. What should you do?
choices: Stay in the lane and go straight through the intersection
Go straight from this lane only when the light is green
Stop at the intersection and wait for a chance to merge
Move to another lane before the intersection
explanation: Traffic in a lane marked this way must turn left. Move out of the lane early, when it is safe; if you are still in it at the intersection, you must make the turn.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign mean for the lane it is posted over?
choices: Traffic in this lane may turn right or go straight
Right turns are not allowed from this lane
Traffic in this lane must turn right
The road curves to the right ahead
explanation: An arrow with the word ONLY on a white regulatory sign means the movement shown is required from that lane - here, a right turn.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What may you do from the lane marked with this sign?
choices: Turn left only
Turn left or go straight
Go straight only
Turn right or go straight
explanation: This optional-movement sign shows two arrows, so traffic in the lane may either turn left or continue straight.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: You are in the left lane and want to continue straight through the next intersection. You see this sign. What should you do?
choices: Move out of the left lane before the intersection
Stay in the left lane, which is also for through traffic
Go straight from the left lane after yielding to turning cars
Go straight from the left lane only on a green arrow
explanation: This sign means drivers in the left lane are required to turn left at the next intersection. Signal and change lanes early when it is safe.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: The right lane ends ahead, so traffic in it must merge left
Drivers may turn right on red here without stopping first
Slower traffic should move into the right lane ahead
Drivers in the right lane must turn right ahead
explanation: Drivers in the right lane must turn right. If you want to go straight, move left before the intersection. A lane that ends ahead is shown with a yellow warning sign instead.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: You see this sign. How may drivers use the center lane?
choices: To pass slower vehicles when the way is clear
As a travel lane for emergency vehicles only
For left turns by traffic from both directions
As a travel lane during rush hour, for through traffic
explanation: This sign marks a two-way left-turn lane, shared by drivers going in both directions to make left turns. It is never a passing or travel lane.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: At the times shown, only vehicles with 2 or more people may use it
The lane is only for vehicles with two or more axles at the times shown
Only buses may use the lane, at all times of the day and night
Two lanes merge into one lane during the hours shown
explanation: The diamond symbol and "2+" mark a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. During the posted times, only vehicles with at least two occupants (counting the driver) may use it.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: It is 8:00 a.m. on a Tuesday and you are driving alone in an ordinary gasoline car. May you use the lane with this sign?
choices: Yes, any car may use this lane on weekdays before 9:30 a.m.
Yes, as long as you keep up with the posted speed limit
Yes, but only to pass slower traffic, then move back out
No, at that time it is for vehicles with 2 or more people
explanation: The sign limits the lane to vehicles with two or more occupants from 6:30 to 9:30 a.m., Monday through Friday. A solo driver may use it only outside those hours.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (lane-use and turn signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.22, PA p.15-16, TX p.34-36)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: Bicyclists may share the full travel lane with cars
Bicycles are not allowed on this road
The lane is reserved for bicyclists
This is a bike route; follow it to reach a bike path
explanation: This sign marks a lane reserved for bicyclists. Do not drive or park in it except where your state allows, such as when preparing to turn, and always yield to bicyclists in it.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: You may pass, but only on the right side of the vehicle ahead
You may not cross the center line to pass other vehicles here
You may pass here if no oncoming traffic is in sight
Other drivers may not pass you, but you may pass them
explanation: This sign marks a no-passing zone, usually where hills, curves or intersections limit how far ahead you can see. Do not pass until the zone ends.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You are behind a car going 10 mph under the speed limit where this sign is posted. What should you do?
choices: Stay behind it until the zone ends and passing is safe
Pass quickly if no oncoming traffic is visible ahead
Pass on the right shoulder if it is wide and paved
Flash your headlights until the driver pulls over to let you by
explanation: Passing is not allowed anywhere in the zone, even when the road ahead looks clear. Be patient and pass only after the zone ends and you have enough clear road.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: You may pass only on the right side of slower vehicles
Passing is not allowed for the next stretch of road
Watch for vehicles passing you on the left
You may pass other vehicles when it is safe to do so
explanation: This sign tells you passing is allowed again. You are still responsible for making sure there is enough clear road ahead before you pass.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: Where is this sign usually posted?
choices: At the start of a no-passing zone
Just before a one-lane bridge
At the end of a no-passing zone
At a freeway entrance ramp
explanation: It marks the end of a no-passing zone. The start of a no-passing zone is marked by the DO NOT PASS sign and, on the left side, a yellow pennant-shaped sign.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You are driving slower than the vehicles around you on a multilane road where this sign is posted. What should you do?
choices: Use the left lane
Use the right lane
Speed up beyond the limit to match traffic
Drive on the shoulder
explanation: This sign asks slower drivers to stay in the right lane and leave the left lane(s) for passing. You never have to exceed the speed limit.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign require?
choices: Trucks must travel in the right lane
Trucks may not use the right lane
Cars must yield to trucks entering from the right
Trucks must take the next exit on the right
explanation: This regulatory sign requires trucks to stay in the right lane on a multilane road.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign tell you?
choices: The road ahead curves to the right, so slow down
The right lane ends ahead
You must turn right at the next intersection ahead
Keep to the right of the island or obstacle ahead
explanation: This sign is placed at the start of a traffic island, median or obstruction. The arrow shows you must pass to the right of it.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign tell you?
choices: The road ahead curves to the left, so slow down
Only left turns are allowed from this lane ahead
Keep to the left of the island or obstacle ahead
The left lane ends ahead, so merge to the right
explanation: This sign marks an island or obstruction that traffic must pass on the left side, as the arrow shows.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: On a multilane highway with this sign, when should you use the left lane?
choices: Whenever traffic is light
Only to pass other vehicles
Whenever you are driving at the speed limit
Only when you plan to exit
explanation: The sign means drive in the right lane and use the left lane only for passing, then move back right.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: You may not enter the road from this direction
Stop first, then enter the road when traffic is clear
The road ahead is closed for construction work
Yield to traffic entering from the side road ahead
explanation: This red-and-white square sign means do not enter: traffic on the road or ramp beyond it is coming toward you. It is common at the wrong end of one-way streets and freeway exit ramps.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: Where is this sign usually posted?
choices: At the start of a freeway on-ramp, before you merge
At a railroad crossing that has no gates or lights
At the start of a school zone near a school
At the wrong end of a one-way street or exit ramp
explanation: It is posted where entering would put you against the flow of traffic, such as the end of a one-way street or an off-ramp seen from the cross street.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You see this sign facing you after turning onto a ramp. What does it mean?
choices: You must turn right at the next intersection on the ramp
The ramp is closed ahead for repairs, so follow the detour
You are driving the wrong way, against traffic
You took the wrong exit and should continue to the next one
explanation: This sign means you are driving against the flow of traffic on a one-way road or ramp. It is placed beyond the DO NOT ENTER sign to warn drivers who have already entered.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: Late at night you pass this sign and see headlights coming toward you in your lane. What should you do?
choices: Keep driving forward until you reach the next exit ramp
Pull out of the travel lane and turn around when safe
Speed up so you spend as little time as possible on the ramp
Stop in your lane and wait for the other car to go around you
explanation: You are traveling the wrong way. Get out of the path of oncoming traffic as quickly and safely as possible, then turn around or wait for help. Continuing ahead risks a head-on crash.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: Trucks are not allowed on this road
Trucks enter or cross the road ahead
Trucks must use the right lane
Truck parking area ahead
explanation: A red circle and slash over a truck means trucks are prohibited. A yellow diamond showing a truck would instead warn of trucks crossing.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: Who may NOT use the road or path where this sign is posted?
choices: People walking on foot
Motor vehicle drivers
People riding bicycles
explanation: This sign closes the road or path to motor vehicles. It is often posted at the entrance to a path for pedestrians and bicyclists.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: A bike lane begins ahead
Bicyclists cross the road ahead
Bicycles are not allowed
Bicyclists may use the full lane
explanation: A red circle and slash over a bicycle means bicycles are prohibited on this road or facility.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: This sign is usually found where?
choices: At a school crosswalk
At a freeway entrance ramp
At the entrance to a park
At the start of a bike path
explanation: Pedestrians, bicycles and motor-driven cycles are typically banned from freeways, so this sign is posted at freeway entrances.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: Traffic on this street flows only in the arrow's direction
Drivers on this street must turn right at the next corner
The road ahead turns sharply to the right, so slow down
Follow the posted detour route to the right
explanation: This black-and-white sign marks a one-way street. Driving the opposite way risks a head-on crash. A yellow arrow sign, by contrast, warns of a sharp turn.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You are stopped at a cross street, and this sign is posted on the far side of the cross street. Which turn onto the cross street is legal?
choices: A left turn
Either a left or a right turn
No turn; you must go straight
A right turn
explanation: The arrow shows that traffic on the cross street flows to your right. Turning left would put you against traffic on a one-way street.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: You are on a side road and see this sign before you reach a highway. What does it tell you?
choices: The highway ahead becomes a two-way road
The divided highway ends just ahead
You are about to cross a divided highway
Two roads merge into one road ahead
explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead is a divided highway. Traffic on the near roadway comes from your left, and traffic on the far roadway comes from your right. The yellow DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS warning sign is different.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: This sign is placed on the center island of a roundabout, facing traffic that is entering. What does it tell you?
choices: Turn left and travel clockwise around the center island
Travel to the right, counterclockwise around the island
Stop before entering the circle, then turn right
Keep to the left of the island as you go around it
explanation: In a roundabout, traffic always circulates counterclockwise, passing to the right of the center island. This sign points entering drivers to the right.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B; state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.14-16, TX p.32-36, FL p.55)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: Parking is never allowed along this part of the curb
Parking is allowed here for a limited time only
Parking is banned only at night, in the direction shown
Only delivery vehicles may park here, in the arrow's direction
explanation: This sign prohibits parking at all times. The arrow shows which part of the curb the restriction covers.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (parking signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, CA p.42)

prompt: Who may park in a space marked with this sign?
choices: Anyone, for up to 15 minutes with hazard lights on
Any driver who stays inside the car with the engine running
Delivery vehicles that are loading or unloading goods
Only vehicles showing a valid disability placard or plate
explanation: The space is reserved for vehicles with a valid disability placard or plate. Parking there without one is illegal, even for a short time.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (parking signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, CA p.42)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: A parking area is ahead
Parking is for permit holders only
Parking is not allowed here
Paid parking zone
explanation: A red circle and slash over the letter P means no parking.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (parking signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. PA p.16, CA p.42)

prompt: Who is this sign meant for, and what does it tell them?
choices: Drivers: keep to the left of pedestrians on the road
Pedestrians: walk on the left, facing traffic
Bicyclists: ride on the left side, facing traffic
Pedestrians: walk on the right side, with traffic
explanation: Where there is no sidewalk, pedestrians should walk on the left, facing traffic, so they can see approaching vehicles. Bicyclists, by contrast, must ride with traffic.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: What does this sign tell pedestrians?
choices: Cross the street only within marked crosswalks
Cross anywhere along the block when no cars are coming
The crosswalk ahead is closed
Wait for a walk signal before crossing
explanation: This sign requires pedestrians to cross only at marked crosswalks along this stretch of road.
ref: MUTCD Sec. 2B (pedestrian and bicycle signs); state driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.23-24, FL p.70, PA p.16)

prompt: What does this sign mean?
choices: A pedestrian crossing is ahead
Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing here
This area is for pedestrians only
Pedestrians may not cross the street here
explanation: The slashed walking figure prohibits pedestrian crossing at this location. A yellow or yellow-green diamond with a walking figure would instead warn of a pedestrian crossing.
